author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Mecka AI is nearing a financing led by Sequoia Capital that would value the robot-training-data company at about $500 million, TechCrunch reported, citing two people familiar with the talks. The exact size of the round was not reported, and the terms were described as unfinished and subject to change.

The proposed deal follows only three months after Mecka announced a $60 million round led by Framework Ventures, with Menlo Ventures, SV Angel and Kindred Ventures participating. The short interval highlights investor demand for companies supplying real-world data used to train humanoid robots and other physical artificial-intelligence systems.

Founded in 2024, Mecka pays people to record everyday tasks using body sensors and smartphones, then organizes that motion data for robotics development. The company has not disclosed its customers. Because the latest financing remains under discussion, the reported valuation should be read as a proposed deal level rather than a completed transaction or live market price.
dek: The proposed financing comes three months after the robot-training-data startup announced a $60 million raise.
headline: Mecka AI nears $500 million valuation in reported Sequoia-led round
